intro: Welcome back! Today you learn to compare things: cheaper, more expensive, the best, and as big as. It's very useful for travel and shopping. Warm-up: Jakarta or Bandung, which city is bigger?
teachingNotes: Indonesian says 'lebih … daripada' and 'paling', so learners translate word by word: *'more big', *'more bigger', *'the most cheap'. Stress that -er already means 'lebih' and -est already means 'paling': bigger (not more big), the cheapest (not the most cheap). Never use more/most together with -er/-est.

Short or long is counted in syllables (suku kata = sound beats), not letters. Indonesian reads every written vowel, so learners count 'nice' as ni-ce or 'large' as lar-ge; both are one beat. Rule taught here: 1 syllable → -er/-est; 2 syllables ending in -y → -ier/-iest (easier, the busiest); other 2-syllable words and longer words → more/most (more famous, the most expensive). A few 2-syllable words take both forms (quiet, clever, simple, narrow): don't use them in exercises; if the learner asks, say both are fine and they meet them later.

Spelling: +r/+st after -e (nicer, the largest); double the last letter after one vowel letter + one consonant letter (bigger, hotter, thinner) but not after two vowel letters (cheaper) or after w (newer); consonant + y → -ier/-iest (easier, happier). good/better/the best and bad/worse/the worst are exceptions to remember (*'gooder', *'more good', *'baddest').

Comparatives take 'than', never 'from' (*'Bali is smaller from Java'): 'daripada' is than. After than, 'than me' is the normal spoken form; accept 'than I am' too. Superlatives need 'the' (*'Jakarta is biggest city') and usually 'in' + place or group (the biggest city in Indonesia); with my/your there is no the (my best friend).

as + plain adjective + as = Indonesian se- (as tall as = setinggi). Never -er inside it (*'as taller as') and never than/like (*'as tall than'). not as … as means 'less': Bandung isn't as hot as Jakarta = Jakarta is hotter.

Limits: the learner has only A1 grammar. No past simple (except was/were), no will, no present perfect. Don't teach far/further/farther, less/least, the + comparative, the + comparative, comparative adverbs (more slowly) or 'as many as'. Use present sentences about real places, prices and people.

keyPoints.title: Compare two things: -er / more … than
keyPoints.explanation: Short words (1 syllable) add -er: cheap → cheaper. Words with 2 syllables ending in -y change y to i: easy → easier. Longer words use more: more expensive. Then use than (not from): Jakarta is bigger than Bandung. -er already means 'lebih', so never say more big or more bigger. good → better and bad → worse are exceptions.

examples.en: A taxi is more expensive than an ojek.
This phone is better than my old phone.
examples.id: HP ini lebih bagus daripada HP lamaku.

id.title: Membandingkan dua hal: -er / more … than
id.explanation: Kata pendek (1 suku kata) ditambah -er: cheap → cheaper. Kata 2 suku kata yang berakhiran -y, y-nya jadi i: easy → easier. Kata yang lebih panjang memakai more: more expensive. Lalu pakai than (bukan from): Jakarta is bigger than Bandung. -er sudah berarti 'lebih', jadi jangan bilang more big atau more bigger. good → better dan bad → worse adalah pengecualian.

keyPoints.title: The most: the -est / the most …
keyPoints.explanation: To say 'paling', use the + -est for short words (the cheapest, the biggest) and the + most for long words (the most expensive). Don't forget the. Often add in + place or group: the biggest city in Indonesia. Exceptions: good → the best, bad → the worst.

examples.en: This is the cheapest hotel in town.
examples.id: Ini hotel paling murah di kota ini.

examples.en: Jakarta is the biggest city in Indonesia.
examples.id: Jakarta adalah kota terbesar di Indonesia.

examples.en: Monday is the worst day of the week.
examples.id: Senin adalah hari paling buruk dalam seminggu.

id.title: Paling: the -est / the most …
id.explanation: Untuk 'paling', pakai the + -est untuk kata pendek (the cheapest, the biggest) dan the + most untuk kata panjang (the most expensive). Jangan lupa the. Sering ditambah in + tempat atau kelompok: the biggest city in Indonesia. Pengecualian: good → the best, bad → the worst.

keyPoints.title: as … as and not as … as
keyPoints.explanation: as + adjective + as means two things are the same, like Indonesian se-: as tall as = setinggi. Use the plain adjective, with no -er. not as … as means 'less': Bandung isn't as hot as Jakarta = Jakarta is hotter.

examples.en: Sari is as old as Dimas.
Bandung isn't as hot as Jakarta.
The bus isn't as fast as the train.

id.title: as … as dan not as … as
id.explanation: as + kata sifat + as artinya dua hal sama, seperti awalan se- dalam bahasa Indonesia: as tall as = setinggi. Pakai kata sifat biasa, tanpa -er. not as … as artinya 'kurang': Bandung isn't as hot as Jakarta = Jakarta lebih panas.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with the right form of 'big': Jakarta is ___ than Bandung.
guidedPractice.hint: Big has one syllable and ends in one vowel + one consonant, so double the g.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with the right form of 'comfortable': In the rain, a car is ___ than a motorbike.
Write the missing word: Bali is smaller ___ Java.
Complete with the right form of 'cheap': This is ___ hotel in town.
guidedPractice.hint: Cheap is a short word. Don't forget the.

guidedPractice.prompt: Sari is 25. Dimas is 25 too. Complete with as … as and 'old': Sari is ___ Dimas.
guidedPractice.hint: They are the same age. Use the plain adjective between the two as.

independentPractice.prompt: Complete with the right form of 'bad': The traffic in Jakarta is ___ than the traffic in Solo.
Write one sentence with these words: Lake Toba / big / lake / in Indonesia.
expected: lake toba is the biggest lake in indonesia
lake toba is the largest lake in indonesia
independentPractice.hint: the + big + -est, and double the g.

independentPractice.prompt: The ojek is faster than the bus. Say the same idea with not as … as: The bus ___.
expected: isn't as fast as the ojek
is not as fast as the ojek
independentPractice.hint: Start with isn't, then as fast as.

assessment.prompt: It's 31°C in Surabaya and 22°C in Bandung. Complete with the right form of 'hot': Surabaya is ___ than Bandung.
assessment.rubric: Correct: hotter (one vowel + one consonant, so double the t). 'hoter' = 70 (right idea, spelling mistake). 'more hot' or 'more hotter' = 20. 'hottest' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Budi's bag is 8 kg. Rina's bag is 5 kg. Complete with the right form of 'heavy': Budi's bag is ___ than Rina's bag.
acceptableAnswers: budi's bag is heavier than rina's bag
assessment.rubric: Correct: heavier (consonant + y → -ier). 'heavyer' = 70 (right idea, spelling mistake). 'more heavy' = 30. 'lighter' = 0 (wrong meaning).

assessment.prompt: Rina loves this book, but she thinks the film is boring. Complete with the right form of 'interesting': For Rina, this book is ___ than the film.
acceptableAnswers: for rina this book is more interesting than the film
assessment.rubric: Correct: more interesting (a long word: in-te-res-ting). 'interestinger' or 'more interestinger' = 20. 'the most interesting' = 20 (that's 'paling', but there are only two things).

assessment.prompt: Puncak Jaya is 4,884 m high. No mountain in Indonesia is higher. Complete with the right form of 'high': Puncak Jaya is ___ mountain in Indonesia.
acceptableAnswers: puncak jaya is the highest mountain in indonesia
assessment.rubric: Correct: the highest. Also accept 'the tallest'. 'highest' without the = 70. 'the most high' = 30. 'higher' = 10.

assessment.prompt: Everybody in the office loves Bu Ani's nasi goreng. Complete with the right form of 'good': Bu Ani makes ___ nasi goreng in the office.
acceptableAnswers: bu ani makes the best nasi goreng in the office
assessment.rubric: Correct: the best (good is an exception). 'best' without the = 70. 'the goodest' or 'the most good' = 20. 'better' = 20.

assessment.prompt: A plane ticket to Bali costs Rp 1.500.000. A ticket to Lombok costs Rp 1.200.000. Complete with as … as and 'expensive': The ticket to Lombok isn't ___ the ticket to Bali.
acceptableAnswers: the ticket to lombok isn't as expensive as the ticket to bali
the ticket to lombok is not as expensive as the ticket to bali
assessment.rubric: Correct: as expensive as. 'as more expensive as' or 'as expensive than' = 40. 'more expensive than' = 0 (wrong meaning: the Lombok ticket is cheaper).

assessment.prompt: Pak Hasan's shop and Bu Ani's shop both have about 100 customers a day. Complete with as … as and 'busy': Pak Hasan's shop is ___ Bu Ani's shop.
acceptableAnswers: pak hasan's shop is as busy as bu ani's shop
assessment.rubric: Correct: as busy as. 'as busier as' or 'as busy than' = 40. 'busier than' or 'not as busy as' = 0 (wrong meaning: the two shops are the same).

blocks.text:
In Indonesian you put **lebih** before the word: *lebih murah*, *lebih mahal*. English does it in two ways, and the length of the word decides:
- **Short words** get **-er** at the end: cheap → **cheaper**, old → **older**.
- **Long words** get **more** in front: expensive → **more expensive**.

Then use **than** for *daripada*: **A bus is cheaper than a taxi.** Never use *from* here.

How long is a word? We count **syllables** (*suku kata*): the beats of sound in a word. Clap once for every beat: **cheap** (1 clap), **ea-sy** (2), **ex-pen-sive** (3).
- **1 syllable** → **-er**: cheap → cheaper, tall → taller.
- **2 syllables ending in -y** → **-ier**: easy → easier, busy → busier.
- **Other words with 2 syllables or more** → **more**: famous → more famous, beautiful → more beautiful.

id.text:
Dalam bahasa Indonesia kamu menaruh **lebih** di depan kata: *lebih murah*, *lebih mahal*. Bahasa Inggris punya dua cara, dan panjang katanya yang menentukan:
- **Kata pendek** diberi **-er** di belakang: cheap → **cheaper**, old → **older**.
- **Kata panjang** diberi **more** di depan: expensive → **more expensive**.

Lalu pakai **than** untuk *daripada*: **A bus is cheaper than a taxi.** Jangan pakai *from* di sini.

Bagaimana tahu panjang sebuah kata? Kita hitung **suku kata** (syllable): ketukan bunyi dalam satu kata. Tepuk tangan sekali untuk setiap ketukan: **cheap** (1 tepukan), **ea-sy** (2), **ex-pen-sive** (3).
- **1 suku kata** → **-er**: cheap → cheaper, tall → taller.
- **2 suku kata berakhiran -y** → **-ier**: easy → easier, busy → busier.
- **Kata lain dengan 2 suku kata atau lebih** → **more**: famous → more famous, beautiful → more beautiful.

rows.id: bagus / enak → lebih bagus / lebih enak

id.note: 1 suku kata: 'nais', huruf e tidak dibaca

rows.en: A bus is cheaper than a taxi.

blocks.text:
Count the sounds, not the letters. In Indonesian every vowel letter is read, so *nice* looks like 'ni-ce' and *large* like 'lar-ge'. But in English the e at the end is silent: **nice** ('nais') and **large** ('laaj') are only **1 syllable**, so they take -er: **nicer**, **larger**.

And don't use both ways together. **-er already means *lebih***: Jakarta is **bigger** than Bandung, not 'more big' or 'more bigger'.

id.text:
Hitung bunyinya, bukan hurufnya. Dalam bahasa Indonesia setiap huruf vokal dibaca, jadi *nice* kelihatan seperti 'ni-ce' dan *large* seperti 'lar-ge'. Tapi dalam bahasa Inggris huruf e di akhir tidak dibaca: **nice** ('nais') dan **large** ('laaj') hanya **1 suku kata**, jadi pakai -er: **nicer**, **larger**.

Dan jangan pakai dua cara sekaligus. **-er sudah berarti *lebih***: Jakarta is **bigger** than Bandung, bukan 'more big' atau 'more bigger'.

blocks.text: A few words with 2 syllables can take both forms (quiet → quieter or more quiet). You'll meet them later. In this lesson, follow the three rules above.

id.text: Ada sedikit kata 2 suku kata yang bisa memakai dua bentuk (quiet → quieter atau more quiet). Kamu akan bertemu kata-kata itu nanti. Di pelajaran ini, ikuti tiga aturan di atas.

blocks.explain: After a comparative (older, cheaper, more expensive) we use **than** = *daripada*. 'from' is a word-by-word translation of *dari*, and 'as' goes in as … as.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: My sister is older ___ me.
id.explain: Setelah bentuk perbandingan (older, cheaper, more expensive) kita pakai **than** = *daripada*. 'from' adalah terjemahan kata per kata dari *dari*, dan 'as' dipakai di as … as.

material.title: Spelling: bigger, nicer, easier, and two exceptions

blocks.text:
Most short words just add **-er** (and **-est** for 'paling'). Three spelling changes:
- Word ends in **e** → add only **-r / -st**: nice → nicer → the nicest.
- Word ends in **one vowel letter + one consonant letter** (b-**i-g**, h-**o-t**) → **double the last letter**: big → bigger → the biggest. This keeps the short vowel sound. *cheap* has two vowel letters (e-a), so no double: cheaper. Never double **w**: new → newer.
- Word ends in **consonant + y** → **y becomes i**: easy → easier → the easiest, happy → happier.

**Exceptions to remember:** good and bad change completely. There's no rule, you just learn them:
- **good → better → the best**
- **bad → worse → the worst**

id.text:
Kebanyakan kata pendek cukup ditambah **-er** (dan **-est** untuk 'paling'). Ada tiga perubahan ejaan:
- Kata berakhiran **e** → tambah **-r / -st** saja: nice → nicer → the nicest.
- Kata berakhiran **satu huruf vokal + satu huruf konsonan** (b-**i-g**, h-**o-t**) → **huruf terakhir digandakan**: big → bigger → the biggest. Ini supaya bunyi vokalnya tetap pendek. *cheap* punya dua huruf vokal (e-a), jadi tidak digandakan: cheaper. Huruf **w** tidak pernah digandakan: new → newer.
- Kata berakhiran **konsonan + y** → **y jadi i**: easy → easier → the easiest, happy → happier.

**Pengecualian yang harus dihafal:** good dan bad berubah total. Tidak ada aturannya, cukup dihafal:
- **good → better → the best**
- **bad → worse → the worst**

rows.id: kurus / tipis → lebih kurus → paling kurus
sibuk / ramai → lebih sibuk → paling sibuk
baik / bagus → lebih baik → paling baik

blocks.text: Not 'gooder', 'more good', 'badder' or 'more bad'. If you only remember two exceptions from this lesson, remember these: **better** and **worse**.

id.text: Bukan 'gooder', 'more good', 'badder' atau 'more bad'. Kalau kamu hanya ingat dua pengecualian dari pelajaran ini, ingatlah ini: **better** dan **worse**.

blocks.explain: **easy** has 2 syllables and ends in consonant + y, so y becomes i: **easier**. 'more easier' uses two ways at once: -er already means *lebih*.

id.explain: **easy** punya 2 suku kata dan berakhiran konsonan + y, jadi y berubah jadi i: **easier**. 'more easier' memakai dua cara sekaligus: -er sudah berarti *lebih*.

id.title: Ejaan: bigger, nicer, easier, dan dua pengecualian

material.title: The most: the cheapest, the most expensive, the best

blocks.text:
For **paling** (or *ter-*, like *terbesar*), use **the** + the same rule:
- Short words: **the + -est**: the cheapest, the biggest, the easiest.
- Long words: **the most** + word: the most expensive, the most beautiful.
- Exceptions: **the best**, **the worst**.

We use it for one thing out of a group of three or more, often with **in** + a place or group: **the biggest city in Indonesia**, **the best student in the class**.

id.text:
Untuk **paling** (atau *ter-*, seperti *terbesar*), pakai **the** + aturan yang sama:
- Kata pendek: **the + -est**: the cheapest, the biggest, the easiest.
- Kata panjang: **the most** + kata: the most expensive, the most beautiful.
- Pengecualian: **the best**, **the worst**.

Dipakai untuk satu hal dari kelompok tiga atau lebih, sering dengan **in** + tempat atau kelompok: **the biggest city in Indonesia**, **the best student in the class**.

rows.en: This is the cheapest hotel in town.
rows.id: Ini hotel paling murah di kota ini.

rows.en: Borobudur is the biggest Buddhist temple in the world.
rows.id: Borobudur adalah candi Buddha terbesar di dunia.

rows.en: It's the most beautiful beach in Lombok.
rows.id: Itu pantai paling indah di Lombok.

rows.en: Rina is the best driver in her family.
rows.id: Rina adalah pengemudi terbaik di keluarganya.

blocks.text:
Two traps from Indonesian:
- *paling murah* is **not** 'the most cheap'. cheap is short, so: **the cheapest**. Use **most** only with long words.
- Don't forget **the**: Jakarta is **the** biggest city, not 'Jakarta is biggest city'. With my/your/his/her you don't need the: **my best friend**.

id.text:
Dua jebakan dari bahasa Indonesia:
- *paling murah* **bukan** 'the most cheap'. cheap kata pendek, jadi: **the cheapest**. Pakai **most** hanya untuk kata panjang.
- Jangan lupa **the**: Jakarta is **the** biggest city, bukan 'Jakarta is biggest city'. Dengan my/your/his/her tidak perlu the: **my best friend**.

blocks.explain: expensive is a long word (ex-pen-sive), so it takes **the most**. And 'paling' always needs **the**: 'most expensive restaurant' without the is wrong here.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: This is ___ restaurant in Surabaya.
id.explain: expensive kata panjang (ex-pen-sive), jadi pakai **the most**. Dan 'paling' selalu butuh **the**: 'most expensive restaurant' tanpa the salah di sini.

id.title: Paling: the cheapest, the most expensive, the best

material.title: as … as: the same, or not the same

blocks.text:
**as + adjective + as** says two things are the **same**. It's like Indonesian **se-**: *setinggi* = **as tall as**, *semurah* = **as cheap as**.

Inside it, use the **plain adjective** (tall, big, good), never the -er form, and finish with **as** (not than or like).

**not as … as** (isn't / aren't as … as) means **less**, like *tidak se-*:
- *Bandung tidak sepanas Jakarta.* → **Bandung isn't as hot as Jakarta.** (So Jakarta is hotter.)

id.text:
**as + kata sifat + as** menyatakan dua hal itu **sama**. Mirip awalan **se-** dalam bahasa Indonesia: *setinggi* = **as tall as**, *semurah* = **as cheap as**.

Di dalamnya pakai **kata sifat biasa** (tall, big, good), jangan bentuk -er, dan akhiri dengan **as** (bukan than atau like).

**not as … as** (isn't / aren't as … as) artinya **kurang**, seperti *tidak se-*:
- *Bandung tidak sepanas Jakarta.* → **Bandung isn't as hot as Jakarta.** (Jadi Jakarta lebih panas.)

rows.en: Sari is as old as Dimas.
This bag is as cheap as that bag.
Bandung isn't as hot as Jakarta.
The bus isn't as fast as the train.
My English isn't as good as your English.
rows.id: Bahasa Inggrisku tidak sebagus bahasa Inggrismu.

blocks.text: Common mistakes: 'as taller as' (no -er inside), 'as tall than' (finish with as). And remember the meaning: **not as big as = smaller**.

id.text: Kesalahan yang sering terjadi: 'as taller as' (tidak ada -er di dalamnya), 'as tall than' (akhiri dengan as). Dan ingat artinya: **not as big as = lebih kecil**.

blocks.prompt: My room is as ___ as your room.
blocks.explain: Between the two **as** we use the plain adjective: **as big as** (sebesar). 'bigger' goes with than, and 'biggest' with the.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: My room is as ___ as your room.
id.explain: Di antara dua **as** kita pakai kata sifat biasa: **as big as** (sebesar). 'bigger' dipakai dengan than, dan 'biggest' dengan the.

id.title: as … as: sama, atau tidak sama
